frankfurt.people: Expanded the six-person roster with institutional researchers, Fromm, four-author empirical collaboration, historians of public life and critical interlocutors. Benjamin remains an associate; critics and historians are not counted as Institute members.
frankfurt.works_and_arguments: Neumann gains Behemoth; Marcuse gains Eros and Civilization with the 1966 self-correction separately dated. Horkheimer theory/research, Benjamin historical time and Habermas communication are grounded in precisely scoped primary readings. Fromm and authoritarianism books retain publisher/metadata limits.
frankfurt.internal_distinctions: Seven new approaches distinguish institutional/empirical work, critical research, authoritarianism, political institutions, liberation, feminist criticism and alternative public-sphere programmes; three inherited approaches clarified.
frankfurt.incoming_connections: Named Marx and Weber passages strengthen inherited links. Nietzsche citation, Spivak/Felski terminology, mediated Gramsci, gender criticism and exile assistance add specific routes without inferring doctrinal agreement.
frankfurt.outgoing_connections: Existing memory, culture, political history, Holocaust and psychohistory routes inspected; Winter/Gay evidence preserved. Public-sphere conceptual resources clarified without inventing direct Hunt reception; Benjamin historicism polemic specifies a particular target.
frankfurt.evidence_and_interpretation: Ten sources added and prior Benjamin primary source scope expanded. Complete Habermas encyclopedia article, Hohendahl introduction and Marcuse preface distinguished from selected Horkheimer, culture-industry, Fraser and Jay readings. All existing IDs, prose and edge classifications preserved; no universal claims endorsed.

frankfurt: Public-sphere historian reception: Fraser supplies mediated Landes/Ryan/Eley readings, but the originals and a direct Habermas-to-Hunt 1984 passage remain unread; inspect available primary introductions before asserting those routes.
